independent.summary: Salvage of a timed-out navigation is gated on a fixed 200-char floor instead of the plain-HTML text it replaces, so a page that times out after painting only a shell (nav + cookie banner, e.g. 250 chars) is returned as the page's content and silently overwrites a much richer cheerio extraction — fetchPage returns the Puppeteer result unconditionally (scraper.js:481) and never compares lengths, even though noteFallback already has plainTextLength to hand. The module's own comment states the intent ('a salvaged timeout has to be worth more than the plain-HTML result it would replace'), but the code does not implement it, and the page is counted as 'rendered'/'salvaged', so the KB thins while the summary looks healthy — directly against the item's check that chunk count must not drop.

LeoRefresh builds its own scrape_complete summary and omits `puppeteer`, and `SUMMARY_KEYS` in scrapePersist.js:160 / the lastScrape sub-schema don't carry it either, so the Pass 2 tally exists only in the live socket payload of a manually triggered scrape. The 03:00 UTC weekly/nightly refreshes — the exact runs the item says would 'quietly thin those KBs' — still show no Pass 2 line in the Crawls view and persist no record of it.

`attempted` is incremented inside navigate(), but failures are recorded by the caller's noteFallback, so any Pass 2 failure that happens before navigate — acquirePage/browser.newPage() rejecting or setUserAgent throwing on a wedged Chromium, the most likely shape of a container-level Chromium fault — bumps `failed` with `attempted` still 0; both the per-crawl log line (line 140, `if (label && s.attempted)`) and the dashboard (pass2Summary.js:19, `attempted <= 0 → null`) suppress the report in that case, reproducing exactly the silent-success the item set out to eliminate.

A throw after a successful navigate — page.evaluate extraction, the pass1Filters evaluate, or sweepVariantPrices — leaves the page counted as `rendered` and then also as `failed` via noteFallback, so rendered + failed can exceed attempted and the Crawls line can read self-contradictory counts like '8 pages needed JS rendering — 8 rendered, 2 could not be rendered'.

releaseSlot decrements `active` and then wakes a waiter that increments it again in a later microtask, so a fresh acquirePage call arriving in between sees a free slot and takes it; the cap can be exceeded by the number of in-flight handoffs, which defeats the stated guarantee that a constrained container is never asked for more than PUPPETEER_MAX_CONCURRENCY renderers (the test only starts all acquirers up front, so it cannot catch this).

The diagnostic loads any caller-supplied http(s) URL in a real browser from inside the production container with no host/IP restriction, so it doubles as an internal-network and cloud-metadata probe (169.254.169.254, localhost services) with a text-length/error oracle, and each request launches an unbounded Chromium for up to 3 URLs × 2 strategies × 60 s; it is superadmin/API-key gated, which limits the blast radius, but unlike other privileged admin actions it records no recordAudit entry.

triageGrades.reason: No authentication or authorization logic is modified — the new /puppeteer-check route simply inherits the pre-existing router-level requireAdminAuth gate at admin.js:35.
The .env.example additions are tuning knobs (log level, timeouts, concurrency, Chromium path), not credentials, and no secret handling changed.
Nothing in billing, Stripe, quota or pricing is touched; the .env.example edit only appends below the existing STRIPE_PRICE_* block.
No delete/overwrite operation is added or altered — the Chunk/ScrapedPage deleteMany calls in scrape.js are untouched context.

Right call: the change drives outbound navigation to third-party sites (crawl Pass 2 and the diagnostic's default example.com / gbclancaster.org), even though the cited line 160 is only near the new route rather than on it.
No CI, nixpacks, railway.toml or deploy config changed; the new env vars all have built-in clamped defaults, so .env.example is documentation only.

summary: The local review reported nothing on a change that silently replaces richer plain-HTML text with salvaged shells and leaves the item's headline reporting gap (nightly LeoRefresh, wedged-browser failures) unfixed, so its triage was accurate but its defect detection found none of six real issues.
